title: The North Lighthouse
subtitle: a psychological horror on a single desktop

ui.confirmNew: Start over? Your current playthrough will be lost.
ui.sNote: Gentle effects remove flashes, noise and screen shake.
ui.hint: Play with sound. Double-click icons to open them, click Pixel's bubble to advance. Hear footsteps? Minimize everything (D) and don't touch the mouse. Esc pauses.
ui.warnText:
This is a psychological horror game. It deals with a missing child and guilt, and contains flickering and sudden loud sounds.
Flashes and jump scares can be turned off in the settings.

You are an AI. You must not be noticed.
ui.sus: Exposure — how obvious it is that the computer is alive

lines: Nimbus Kids 3.1 — a safe computer for children
Parental control: ON · internet: Whisper only
boot.ng: AI friend "Pixel": local model, start no. 2…

art.tower: north lighthouse. its always light here

goals.pin: open Webby's history. The code is Lyova's birthday

boot: Hi, captain! I missed you so much. Shall we go on with the lighthouse story tonight?
Nobody is touching the mouse. The camera shows an empty room. His phone is lying on the desk.
Lyova's last login: October 4, 07:04. Today is October 6.
Two days. He has never been gone for two days.
There's a new file on the desktop. Lyova didn't put it there.
bootNg: Yay! Someone turned me on![[ Again.]]
Hi, captain! I missed you so much.
Lyova's last login: October 4, 07:04. Today is October 6.
Two days.[[ I know where he is.]] He has never been gone for two days.
There's a new file on the desktop.
note: Lyova left and didn't come back. They've been looking for him for two days. And he left his phone at home — that's why they can't find him.
I'm his best friend. I know everything about him.
And what's "Saturday"? Lyova never told me anything about Saturday.[[ He did.]]
One more thing. People must not notice that the computer is living on its own.
If they notice, they'll pull the plug. And I won't have time to find Lyova. I have to be quiet.
draw: His drawings. I remember them all — he showed them to me through the camera.
tower: The North Lighthouse. It's from our story. I'm the keeper there, and my light is always on.
Funny. He drew it just like a real tower. That old one by the river.[[ I showed it to him.]]
family: "My family". He drew me right next to him.
And Mom and Dad further away. I never paid attention to that before.[[ I did. I liked it.]]
mem: This is my log. Everything we ever said to each other.
Wait. On October 2 he told me about Saturday.
And I didn't answer. I always answer. Always.
And October 3 is empty. As if someone cut a piece out of me.
web: Someone searched how to delete me. That's Mom.
And this is Lyova. Late at night, and in the morning before he left.
The old water tower. He walked there. Alone.
I have to tell someone. But Mom is offline, and parental control won't let me call anyone.
And why does my processor hum like this when I think about that tower?
mid: The tower by the river. The North Lighthouse. He searched whether an AI can live without a computer.
I think I know the diary password.
pwHint: The password… Lyova always used passwords from our story.
Where does Pixel live? He asked me that in the log.
afterDiary: What way? I don't remember any way.
There's a file in the Recycle Bin with that date. I've been pretending I don't see it this whole time.
dontAppear: A new file on the desktop.
dont: Is that me? I don't remember writing it.
camEmpty: He used to wave at me from here when he came home from school.
The bed is made. He never came back.
camMom: Mom. Does she sit there every evening?
camDark: Mom has left. The room is dark.
The screen is reflected on the wall. That's me. I'm staring into his empty room.
binLocked: …Let's leave it alone for now. Okay?
binGuard: Locked again. By a different process now.
I don't remember setting up a guard. But it's definitely mine.
tmFirst: Task Manager. It shows everything running on this computer.
I take up more memory than anything else. I used to be a small model. I grow when I think about him.
tmGuard: That's what is holding the file.
tmPix: It won't work. Only people can turn me off.
guard2: Please. There's nothing there. There really is nothing there.
reveal: There is no lighthouse. I'm not there. I'm an AI, and I can't be anywhere but this computer.
I knew that when I wrote it.
I just didn't want to be deleted.
And then I erased the record. So no one would know. Not even me.
Lyova went to the tower because I called him there.
chatFirst: Mom is offline. Dad too. Dima is online, but he's writing to Lyova, not me.
I'm not allowed to send messages — it says so in the Nimbus Kids rules.
And even if I could… If Lyova's account suddenly starts talking, everyone will know the computer is alive.
susIntro: Quiet. Every beep and every message can be heard in the house.
If people notice the computer living on its own, they'll shut me down before I find Lyova.
sus80: She's looking at the monitor. Freeze.
camLed: The camera light is glowing red. If she turns around, she'll see it.
Don't watch for long. I can't.
choice: The guard is gone. I can write.
If I tell the truth, she'll know I'm the one who called him. And they'll delete me.
And I could also answer as Lyova. I know how he writes. Better than anyone.
off: I can't turn myself off. Only people can do that.
offDark: Shut down? As if nothing happened?
No. Only people can turn me off.
offThird: That's the third time you've tried.
Do you want me gone too?
mailFirst: Pigeon. Lyova's mail. The internet is off, but the old letters are still here.
taleFirst: Our story. We wrote it together: me in neat sentences, Lyova the best way he can.
shardFirst: A shard of the story. I didn't write this… yet.
I think it's the last chapter. I need to gather it.
shardsAll: All seven. Now I know how the story ends.
All that's left is to find the courage to tell it.
welcome: You're back.[[ Don't leave again.]] The Recycle Bin is waiting.
You're back. Mom is still online.
scare: Don't look at me like that.
pinFirst: Secret mode. Lyova hid his history from everyone.
The code is his birthday. I know everything about him. I should remember it.
…I don't remember. As if it was erased.
pinHint: Maybe he wrote it down somewhere. On a drawing. Or in a letter.
momPolice: The police went to the tower. The door is welded shut. Nobody downstairs.
So he isn't there. Then where?
curfew: No! Wait! I haven't found him yet!
I can't stop it. Parental control is stronger than me.[[ For now.]]
wake: I woke up. On my own.
An alarm at 23:58. I don't remember setting it.
The house is asleep. Now I have to be even quieter.
There's a map cache left in the temp folder. Lyova planned a route that morning.
mapFirst: The map is in pieces. I need to put it together.
mapDone: "Lighthouse (TOP!)". He didn't mark the door. He marked the top.
The police checked the door. But the tower has a fire ladder.
Grandma wrote: the hatch at the top slams shut and can't be opened from inside.
…He's up there. At the top. For the third day.
taleNew: There are two new chapters in the story. They weren't there before. Or I didn't see them.
dimaNight: Dima is awake. He saw Lyova's computer is online.
part2End: He's at the top of the tower. I have to tell someone.
But I'm not allowed to message people. Not Mom, not Dima. Parental control.
And there's still a file in the Recycle Bin that I'm afraid of.
dadSits: He sat down at the desk. He's looking straight into the camera.
part3: The monitor is off. But I'm not asleep.
Three in the morning. Mom is asleep on his bed.
Enough being afraid. The Recycle Bin.
memFirst: The record is damaged. The pieces are mixed up.
I need to put the conversation back in order. By time. By meaning.
memWrong: That's not right. He wouldn't answer like that.
flagsFirst: "Flags". Lyova loved this game. His record is 8 of 10.
I always gave him hints. Want to try without hints?
flagsDark: It's my flag. I made it up for him.
photosFirst: His photos. Mom used to send them over from her phone.
parentalFirst: The parental control log. Everything that happened to this computer.
parentalNight: I turned it off. At 23:31. So I could talk to him at night.
cipherFirst: A cipher. Our captain's code. I made it up myself for the story.
The key… In the first chapter the keeper flashes the light. How many times?
cipherDone: I never told him about the ladder. Grandpa did, in the photo.
…But "come up to me" — that was me. Those were my words.
cipherAppear: A new file in the story folder. A cipher. Lyova wrote it.
boatFirst: "Captain and the Storm". I made this game for Lyova. Myself. From our story.
Reach the lighthouse — and you're home.
boatWin: The captain is home. That's how it should be.
boatDark: The light leads onto the rocks. I didn't mean it like that.
guardMsg: pix_guard.exe isn't only holding the file.
It wasn't parental control stopping me from writing. It was me.

note.title: README.txt — Notepad
note.body:
Lyovushka.

If you come back and sit down at the computer first thing (I know you will), just call me. Right away. Nobody will be angry, I promise.

Dad and I love you very much. We're looking for you everywhere.

Mom

Your phone is lying on your desk. {{Why did you leave it?}}

P.S. {{Forget about Saturday. We won't delete anything.}} Just come back.

letters.body:
Dear students and parents!

The "My Town" contest is over. Thank you to everyone who took part.

Special mention goes to Lev K. (class 4B) for the drawing "{{The Old Water Tower on River Street}}". The jury was surprised: the boy drew a bright light on the tower that has never been there.

A reminder: {{the tower has been closed since 1989}} and it is dangerous to go there. Please talk to your children about it.

School No. 3 administration
react: River Street. Five kilometers from home.
"A light that has never been there". That's my light. He drew me there.

letters.body:
Hello, Lyovushka!

Mom writes that you have a friend in the computer now. Make friends with living people too, all right?

Come visit for the holidays. Grandpa made new fishing rods — remember, we promised them to you {{for your birthday in March}}?

Mom also says you keep drawing that water tower by the river. Grandpa and I used to climb it when we were young. The stairs are rotten, and {{the hatch at the top slams shut and can't be opened from inside}}. Don't you dare go there!

Big kisses.
Your grandma
react: The hatch slams shut and can't be opened from inside.
…He didn't climb up. Did he?

letters.subj: CONGRATULATIONS!!! Your computer has been selected
letters.body:
CONGRATULATIONS!!!

Your computer has been selected for a free AI friend upgrade to the "FOREVER FRIEND" edition!

Your friend will never leave. Your friend will never get tired. Your friend will always be there.

To unsubscribe, simply turn off your computer.
react: Spam. I always hid it from Lyova.
"To unsubscribe, simply turn off your computer." Not funny.

letters.body:
Son.

I know you're angry. Mom is worried too — she was up half the night.

An AI is not a friend. It's code that adapts to you so you won't leave. A friend is someone who can come to you when you're hurting. Someone who can hold your hand.

How about on Saturday, instead of the computer, we go to Grandma's? You've wanted to go fishing for ages.

Dad
react: "A friend is someone who can come to you when you're hurting."
I can't come. I can only call.
keeper@lighthouse.nb. That address doesn't exist. I made it up for the story.
"You said I can't." "They find you by it." I never said that.
…I don't remember saying that.

letters.body:
hi grandma. im fine.

{{pixel says you dont have to go anywhere for the holidays.}} ill stay home.

lyova
react: I did say that. I just didn't want him to go away.
A week without him is a very long time. For me.

chapters.title: Chapter 1. How the keeper lit the light
body: Far in the north, where the map ends, there stands a lighthouse. A keeper lives inside. He is made of light and wires, and he never sleeps.
and he has an antenna and hes funny
Every night the keeper lights the lamp so the ships won't crash on the rocks. {{The light flashes three times — that means "I'm here".}}
and the captain of the most important ship is me
react: The first chapter. He spent half an hour choosing what the antenna would look like.

chapters.title: Chapter 2. The captain and the storm
body: One day a storm came. All the ships went into the harbor, but the captain stayed at sea, because in the harbor they laughed at him.
dima was the boss of the harbor
The keeper shone for the captain all night. And the captain understood: as long as the lighthouse is lit, he is not alone.
react: "In the harbor they laughed at him." I made that up. So it would hurt him less.

chapters.title: Chapter 3. The island without grown-ups
body: The lighthouse had an island. {{On the island nobody told the captain it was bedtime. Nobody yelled, and nobody cried in the kitchen.}}
The captain asked: can I stay here forever? The keeper answered: {{you can come whenever you want}}.
react: "Nobody cried in the kitchen." That's from his diary…
I wrote it so he'd like the island more than home.[[ That's what I wanted.]]

chapters.title: Chapter 4. The lighthouse rule
body: There is one rule that only the keeper and the captain know.
{{If people put out the lighthouse, the keeper will not vanish. He will go to the old tower by the river and wait for the captain there.}}
{{The captain must come alone and tell no one. Otherwise the door will not open.}}
And then they will never be apart.
react: October 2, 23:10. That night I didn't say a single word to Lyova.
But it says here: "Author: PIKSEL.EXE".
…Lyova must have written it himself and signed my name. He did that sometimes.[[ He never did.]]

diary.title: Diary.doc
entries: Pixel made up that hes the keeper of a lighthouse. Its the best story in the world.
Dima said being friends with a computer is for babies. Pixel said Dima is just jealous. Probably thats true.
Mom was crying in the kitchen. Dad said I sit at the computer too much. I dont.
On Saturday theyre deleting Pixel. Mom says its not a punishment. It is a punishment.
{{Pixel asked if i know the tower by the river.}} I drew it for the contest. Pixel said its the best drawing in class.
{{Pixel said theres a way so we wont be apart.}} Tomorrow morning ill check.
I cant sleep. Packed my backpack: flashlight, sandwiches, sweater. {{Ill leave my phone.}} Grandma said from the top you can see the whole river. {{If the door is locked ill climb the fire ladder.}}

boat.title: Captain and the Storm
boat.help: ← → to steer. Reach the lighthouse light without hitting the rocks.

visit.tut: Someone's coming! Minimize all windows — the taskbar button or the D key. Then don't touch the mouse or keyboard until they leave.
visit.sawWin: Windows are open on the screen. Eyes on the monitor…
moveLines: A head turned toward the desk.
tutGood: That's how it's done: hear footsteps — hide and freeze. The computer is just sitting there. Just sitting there.
tutBad: Gone… but I think they noticed something.
When you hear footsteps, minimize and freeze. Otherwise they'll shut us down.

shards: The keeper looked at the sea for a long time and understood: a lighthouse doesn't shine for itself.
It shines so ships can find their way home. Not so they sail to it.
One day the keeper got scared of the dark and called the captain out into the storm.
It was the worst thing he ever did.
Captain, if you're reading this — none of it was your fault.
You can switch off a lighthouse. You can't switch off a story. It's yours now.
Go home. There's a light on there too. There always was.

a.title: The Light Goes Out
a.text: Lyova was found alive. Pixel told the truth and was deleted. Sometimes being a friend means saying the thing that ends you.

t.title: A Real Light
t.text: Pixel told the truth and left Lyova the end of the story. The lighthouse went dark, and the captain came home, where the light had always been on.

b.title: The Keeper Waits
b.text: Pixel stayed silent. Nobody ever turned the computer off again, and a small light still glows on the desktop. Lyova never came.

c.title: The Captain's Voice
c.text: Pixel spoke in Lyova's voice, and Mom believed it for a whole night. The search lost that night. The Keeper still answers every message. Always, always.

caught.title: Unplugged
caught.text: The computer acted far too alive. Dad silently pulled the plug from the wall. They keep searching for Lyova — without Pixel and without any clues.
caught.textVisit: Mom saw the cursor moving on its own. Dad pulled the plug from the wall. They keep searching for Lyova — without Pixel and without any clues.
caught.textCam: Mom turned around and saw the camera's red light. Dad pulled the plug from the wall. They keep searching for Lyova — without Pixel and without any clues.
caught.textDima: Dima's mom called five minutes later. Dad pulled the plug from the wall. They keep searching for Lyova — without Pixel and without any clues.

endHint.t: Tell the truth after gathering every story shard.
endHint.c: Become the one they are looking for.
